market_holds: At the seal (18:08 UTC) spot was 152.98. The front-week straddle implies 16.7%, or 14.46% event-only, with skew paying for downside (+4.1 vol pts) and a wide ATM spread (35% of mid), per the sealed baseline. Over seven prior close-to-close reactions the median absolute move was 8.04%, two of them up. Opening gaps over the last 12 prints (my arithmetic on Yahoo bars) are asymmetric: beats opened +2.3% to +6.4% and misses opened -12.4% to -14%. The call is Nov 17 at 11:00 ET, after the scored open, so only the release counts. Consensus for FQ4 is $1.56 EPS (+10.6% y/y) on $335.1M revenue (+12.5% y/y, +7.5% q/q), flat for 60 days (Investing.com, 2026-11-16). The stock has fallen 55% from its 52-week high of $336, in step with an AI-power basket that derated through October and November (POWL -7.5% over 20 days against ETN -13.6%, GEV -15.5%, VRT -8.4%). On the run day POWL rose about 7.5% on thin volume while that basket fell 3-6% and SPY fell about 1.9%: a pre-print pop against the tape. Short interest is about 2.9M shares, roughly 8% of float, with 4 days to cover (Equibles, 2026-11-13). Analyst targets are being cut (JPM 300 to 250, Cantor 235 Neutral), with 4 buy and 3 hold. The line it trades on is near-term conversion: revenue and EPS against consensus, then orders and backlog. Q3 opened -12.7% on a revenue miss despite record orders of $934M.
view: Demand is not the question. Eaton's Electrical Americas segment shows data-center sales +54% and book-to-bill 1.3 for the same Jul-Sep quarter, and Powell's own ex-mega orders ran about $440-530M a quarter in FY26 (Q1 $439M, Q2 $490M, Q3 about $530M ex the $400M+ data-center order). A Q4 book-to-bill of about 1.2-1.6 against roughly $335M of revenue is the likely case, and the market expects it. The question is conversion. Revenue has missed consensus three quarters in a row (Q1 $251M vs about $257M, Q2 a miss per Zacks, Q3 $312M vs about $322M, 'project timing'), and EPS missed in Q2 and Q3. Consensus did not move after the Q3 miss and again asks for a +7.5% sequential step, above the +5.1% Q3 delivered. Gross margin faces copper and aluminum inflation, and SG&A faces costs from the facility ramp, both flagged by the CFO in August. Against that, the 12-month backlog conversion figure rose to $1.3B (from $913M a year earlier, which converted at 1.27x into $1,157M of trailing revenue), Jacintoport was due at fiscal year-end, and Q4 has been seasonally Powell's strongest quarter. So a revenue catch-up is plausible. On balance I see roughly a 55% chance of another revenue or EPS shortfall. The asymmetric opening-gap history says a shortfall costs more at the open than a beat earns, and the 7.5% pop against a falling basket on the run day raises the bar slightly. The 55% derating and the lowered targets mean much disappointment is already in the price, though. I cannot show a mispricing clean enough to bet: a slight lean down, no recommendation.

recommendation.reason: Consensus asks for a +7.5% sequential revenue step from a company that has missed revenue consensus three straight quarters, with copper and ramp-cost headwinds flagged in August. Past misses opened -12% to -14% and beats only +2% to +6%. But the 55% derating, the target cuts and a backlog-conversion figure that supports a catch-up mean I cannot show the price holds the wrong side. A 55/45 lean is below the bar for a bet.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q4 revenue at or above about $345M with gross margin at or above 30.5% and book-to-bill above 1.3 would make the opening gap positive despite the run-day pop.

self_critique: The revenue-miss streak is public and the stock has already derated 55%, so a modest miss may be priced, and a bigger-than-expected Q4 from Jacintoport plus seasonally strong Q4 conversion could beat and gap the stock up. The conversion arithmetic (1.27x on last year's 12-month figure) points that way. The run-day pop may also reflect informed buying ahead of a good print. Tape beta to the AI-power basket at tomorrow's open could swamp the release either way.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped: it separated the basket derating from company news and exposed the idiosyncratic run-day pop. P7's 'estimate the line from its inputs' pushed me into the backlog-conversion arithmetic, which cut both ways and kept me from a forced call.
